article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Morning Brief
article.dek: Thursday night is settled, the cards flipped overnight, and two starting quarterbacks get their answer today.

items.headline: Thursday night is done: Texans 26, Colts 3
paragraphs: C.J. Stroud threw three touchdowns and the Texans rolled the Colts 26-3 on Thursday night. Indianapolis scored on its opening drive and never scored again. Houston held the Colts to 167 total yards.
The Texans covered as 12.5-point favorites, and the game totaled 29 points, well under the 44.5 total. Houston moves to 4-6. The Colts fall to 3-8.

One note on last night's Fade: the tickets were on the Texans moneyline and the money was on the Colts. The tickets side won, and won big. The Fade is decision context, not a pick. It was right to watch, and it would have been wrong to follow blindly.
items.takeaway: Texans 26, Colts 3. Stroud threw three touchdowns, the Colts managed 167 yards, and last night's split resolved with the tickets side.

items.headline: Both cards flipped overnight
paragraphs: Hit Rate is now the Jacksonville Jaguars moneyline at -255 on DraftKings, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET against the Giants. Last night it was the Lions moneyline at -260.
Balanced is still the New York Jets +3, now at -105 on DraftKings for Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET against the Chargers. That is one cent better than last night's -106.
Value is still empty. The app found no +EV price on the board, and it says so plainly instead of forcing one.
items.takeaway: New cards this morning: Hit Rate is Jaguars moneyline -255, Balanced is Jets +3 at -105. Value is still empty.

items.headline: Two starting quarterbacks get their answer today
paragraphs: Baker Mayfield practiced Thursday, limited, and said he feels ready to play Sunday at Detroit. The Bucs decide today, and the final injury designations land today. If he cannot go, rookie Jalon Daniels makes his fourth start. The app still lists Mayfield as Tampa Bay's expected starter.

Geno Smith was limited again Thursday with his ankle injury, but he says the plan is to play Sunday at the Chargers, and an MRI showed no significant damage. Rookie Cade Klubnik is the backup if Smith cannot go. The app still lists Smith as the Jets' expected starter.

Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. missed his second straight practice with an ankle injury, which would thin a Tampa Bay defense that takes the ball away as well as anyone. Final designations land today. Inactives come about 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday.
items.takeaway: Mayfield and Geno Smith both say they plan to play, and both teams decide today. The app lists both as expected starters for now.

items.headline: Weather: still nothing new
paragraphs: The forecast has not been refreshed since Tuesday, and nothing in it has changed since last night. Chicago is still the windiest spot on Sunday: 49 degrees, 15 mph wind with gusts to 32.

Buffalo gets 12 mph wind with gusts to 26. Rain is in the forecast in Philadelphia and at MetLife, and there is a 76% chance of precipitation for the Mexico City game Sunday night. Detroit plays indoors.
items.takeaway: Mild everywhere. Chicago is still the windiest spot at 15 mph with gusts to 32.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: How to read the flipped Hit Rate card
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the Jaguars moneyline at -255. That is the app's most likely winner, not a value play. The app gives Jacksonville about a 76% chance to win, and the play-through price is -264, so -255 is inside the number the app will still take.

The spread tells the same story. Jacksonville is -6.0, and the app's expected margin is Jacksonville by about 5.7. The app basically agrees with the market here. This card is about win probability, and the app says Jacksonville is the most likely winner on the board. Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate is Jaguars moneyline -255: the most likely winner, not a value play. The app agrees with the market on the spread, so this one is about the win, not a gap.

items.headline: Balanced is the same pick at a slightly better price
paragraphs: Balanced is still the Jets +3, now at -105 instead of -106. The app gives the Jets about a coin flip to cover, 50.6%, and the play-through price is -108. That is the middle ground: a strong pick without paying too much.

The Jets are also the team with the quarterback question. Geno Smith says he plans to play, and the app lists him as the expected starter. If your book has the Jets at +3 and Check says bet, that is the number the card is built on.
items.takeaway: Balanced is Jets +3 at -105, a cent better than last night. The app calls it about a coin flip to cover.

items.headline: The app still thinks the big spreads are too fat, and it still bet none of them
paragraphs: Kansas City is -16.5 and the app has the Chiefs by about 6.3. Buffalo is -16.5 and the app has the Bills by about 3.4. Chicago is -11.5 and the app has the Bears by about 0.2. Denver is -10.5 and the app has the Broncos by about 2.2.

Five big spreads, five big gaps, zero cards. A gap is a starting point, not a bet. The app did not bet any of them, and the board says why: the price has to be right, not just the opinion. If your book has one of these favorites cheaper than the app's number, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Five big spreads, five big model gaps, zero cards. The gap alone is not the bet. Check your price.

items.headline: The tickets love Detroit. The money is heavier on Tampa Bay.
paragraphs: Look at the DraftKings moneyline splits for Tampa Bay at Detroit, read this morning. Detroit has 89% of the bets but only 70% of the money. Tampa Bay has 11% of the bets but 30% of the money. The crowd and the bigger money disagree.

The line has already moved toward Tampa Bay once. Detroit was a 7-point favorite on Thursday and is now -6.0, after Mayfield practiced. Another book is paying +220 on the Bucs moneyline while DraftKings lists +212. The disagreement is real, and the market has already started to notice it.
items.takeaway: Most tickets are on Detroit, most money is not. Tampa Bay has 11% of the bets but 30% of the money, and the line already moved from -7 to -6.

items.headline: What to watch, and how to use it
paragraphs: If the public keeps hammering Detroit and the number drifts back toward -6.5 or -7 without any new bad Bucs news, you may be looking at the same football opinion for a better price. That is the spot to wait for.

But the waiting has a deadline. The Bucs decide on Mayfield today. If he is ruled out, the number goes the other way fast, and the better Tampa Bay price disappears. If he plays, the price you are waiting for may never come back. Check your Tampa Bay price against the app before kickoff, and let Check give you the verdict on your number.
This is decision context, not a pick. The app's cards are the Jaguars and the Jets. The Fade is a second layer: it tells you where the price might move, not what to bet.
items.takeaway: Watch the Detroit number: back toward -6.5 or -7 with no new bad Bucs news means Tampa Bay gets cheaper. A Mayfield ruling-out today kills that wait, so check the final designations first.

items.headline: The Hit Rate card changed hands overnight
paragraphs: Last night Hit Rate was the Lions moneyline at -260. This morning it is the Jaguars moneyline at -255. The app's most-likely-winner pick moved to Jacksonville.
Balanced held: Jets +3, with the price one cent better at -105. Value is still empty. The board flipped to a new week of cards, and only the Hit Rate name changed.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate flipped from Lions moneyline -260 to Jaguars moneyline -255 overnight. Balanced held at Jets +3, a cent better.

items.headline: Thursday's split resolved with the tickets
paragraphs: Last night the tickets were on the Texans moneyline and the money was on the Colts. The Texans won 26-3 and covered -12.5. The total landed at 29, under 44.5.

That is the Fade working as designed: it flagged a disagreement, and the disagreement resolved the way the crowd leaned. It is a reminder the Fade is context, not a command. The next split gets judged on its own numbers.
items.takeaway: Last night's Fade split went the tickets' way: Texans 26, Colts 3, covering -12.5 with the total under 44.5.

items.headline: Everything else held still
paragraphs: Kansas City is still -16.5, Buffalo is still -16.5, Cincinnati is still -6.0 for Monday night, and Detroit is still -6.0 after the Mayfield news moved it Thursday. Jacksonville is still -6.0.
No other line on the board moved overnight. When the board is quiet, the morning check is quick: the cards changed, the lines did not.
items.takeaway: No other line moved overnight: KC -16.5, Buffalo -16.5, Cincinnati -6.0, Detroit -6.0, Jacksonville -6.0 all held.

items.headline: Friday is decision day for two quarterbacks
paragraphs: Final injury designations land today for Baker Mayfield and Geno Smith. Both say they plan to play. Both teams decide today.

Check your Tampa Bay and Jets prices against the app's listings now, then check back after the designations. If your book has a good number right now and Check says bet, bet now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number Sunday, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too. Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday, and the board refreshes every morning and evening.
And log the losers too. Settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself.
items.takeaway: Check your Tampa Bay and Jets prices now, then check back after today's final designations. If Check says bet on a good number, bet now. And log the losers.
